class.name: VirtualCamera3D
class.brief_description: A place for the viewport's [Camera3D] to be: following, orbiting, along a path or framing a group.
class.description:
Add virtual cameras to a scene beside an ordinary [Camera3D]. Each frame, every virtual camera works out where it should be and what it should look at, and the viewport's current [Camera3D] takes the pose and [member fov] of the live one: the one with the highest [member priority]. When the live camera changes, the real camera blends from where it was over the new camera's [member blend_time]. [codeblock] func _on_boss_appeared(): $BossCamera.priority = 10 # Blends over to the boss.
func _on_boss_defeated(): $BossCamera.priority = 0 # And back to whichever is next. [/codeblock] The real camera is moved after every node's [method Node._process], so it shows where targets are that frame, and between physics ticks where they move in them. The virtual camera node itself moves to where it should be, so it can be seen in the remote scene tree and other nodes can follow it. In VR the headset moves the camera, so an [XRCamera3D] is left alone.

method.name: get_focus_distance
method.description: How far away what it keeps in focus is now, in meters, eased by [member focus_damping].

method.name: is_live
method.description: Whether the real camera is following this one.

method.name: shake
method.description: Shakes the camera, turning it by up to a few degrees at a [param strength] of [code]1.0[/code], fading over [param duration] seconds. A weaker shake doesn't cut short a stronger one.

method.name: snap
method.description: Puts the camera where it should be at once on the next frame, without [member follow_damping] or [member look_damping]: after teleporting its target, say.

members.member: How the blend to this camera eases, with [member blend_transition].
How long the real camera takes to move over when this camera becomes live. [code]0[/code] cuts.
The curve of the blend to this camera, as a [Tween]'s.
How see-through what's in the way becomes, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].

If [code]true[/code], while it's live, what stands between it and its [member follow_target] fades out (as [member GeometryInstance3D.transparency]) so the player stays in sight, and back in once it's out of the way. What counts is any body on [member orbit_collision_mask] a line from the target to the camera passes through: the meshes under it, and the mesh it's under.
How blurred what's out of focus is, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].
The physics layers [constant FOCUS_CENTER] focuses on.
Seconds the focus takes to settle on a new distance, as a camera's autofocus does.

What it keeps in focus, with depth of field round it: nothing, what's in the middle of the view, or its target. The real camera's [CameraAttributesPractical] (made for it if it has none) take the focus while this camera is live, and are given back when it isn't.
How slowly it catches up with where it should be, in seconds: about how long it takes to cover most of the way. [code]0[/code] keeps up exactly.
How it moves: see [enum FollowMode].

With [constant FOLLOW_TARGET], where it sits from the target. With [constant FOLLOW_ORBIT], where the point it orbits sits from the target (raise it to orbit a character's head). With [constant FOLLOW_PATH], added to the point on the path. With [constant FOLLOW_GROUP], the direction it looks at the group from, and its least distance.
With [constant FOLLOW_PATH], the [Path3D] it moves along.
The node it follows.
With [constant FOLLOW_GROUP], the nodes it keeps in view.
The real camera's field of view while this one is live, in degrees.
A node it turns to face. Without one, an orbit faces the point it orbits, a path camera its target and a group camera the group's middle; other cameras keep their own rotation.
How slowly it turns to face what it looks at, in seconds. [code]0[/code] keeps up exactly.

With [constant FOLLOW_ORBIT], the physics layers that block the camera: it moves in front of anything on them between it and its target at once, and eases back out with [member follow_damping]. The target, and the body it's on (when it's a point on a character), don't block it. [code]0[/code] goes through everything.
With [constant FOLLOW_ORBIT], how far it stays from the point it orbits.
With [constant FOLLOW_ORBIT], how far above (negative) or below it looks at the target, in radians. Set it from the player's input to let them look round.
With [constant FOLLOW_ORBIT], which way round the target it is, in radians: [code]0[/code] is behind along +Z.

The live camera is the one with the highest priority in its viewport, among those that can process (see [member Node.process_mode]). On a tie, the one that entered the tree or changed priority last wins.

signal.name: live_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the camera becomes live, or stops being live.

constants.constant: Stays where it's put, for a fixed camera. It can still turn to [member look_at_target].
Keeps [member follow_offset] from [member follow_target], facing the way it's turned (or towards [member look_at_target]).
Circles [member follow_target] at [member orbit_distance], [member orbit_pitch] and [member orbit_yaw], facing it: a third-person camera.
Stays on [member follow_path] at the point closest to [member follow_target], facing it: a camera on a rail.
Keeps every node in [member follow_targets] in view, backing off along [member follow_offset] as they spread out.
No depth of field from it.
Focuses on what's in the middle of the view: the first thing on [member focus_collision_mask] straight ahead.
Focuses on [member look_at_target], or else [member follow_target].
